title: BREE prospect ranking
subtitle: Ranked by the value claims, forensic quantum, delay and Building Safety Act 2022 practice would bring to each organisation.

prospects.organisation: Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea
prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Treadgold House decarbonisation matter at scoping stage with claim value TBC, Touchstone instructed to value by end October 2026 and an adjudication planned for December 2026.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse. Note also the separate RBKC PCSA and Fusion 21 call-off contracts with United Living.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Two live Points Cross matters (Blocks A&B and Block C) with a £3m smash-and-grab already secured against it and an EOT and final account submission expected by around October 2026.
prospects.routeInNote: Directly adverse. Not approachable while Points Cross is live.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: 222 buildings require remediation, 94 complete, 17 underway; over £250m committed and over £20m spent on waking watch. States it is pursuing developers, insurers and government funds. Governance downgraded G1 to G2 on 27 August 2025. No consolidated provision published.
prospects.routeInNote: Recovery against developers and original contractors, and quantification of the unprovided liability. Latent conflict via Wandsworth Exchange and Quadrant Construction Services.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Welbourne: BREE pursuing c.£22m of final account and EOT recovery (a final account submitted 31 January 2025 seeking a further £18.2m) with a £3.7m LD counterclaim to defend, PAP held 3 December 2025 and Court proceedings issued.
prospects.routeInNote: The largest single adverse position in the portfolio.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Revenue £498m and pre-tax profit £31.7m in the year to March 2026, order book £2.8bn, debt free with no borrowing. HS2 (EKFB, SCS), AMP8 water and Sizewell C. No reported disputes and low BSA exposure.
prospects.routeInNote: The natural need is NEC compensation event, disruption and delay analysis on HS2 and AMP8, which is squarely your practice. BREE commenced adjudication against them on Points Cross from 1 July 2026.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Structural defects claim with remedials priced on full external wall replacement, a £4m consequential loss claim under review by Mark Lill, and legal proceedings already started against BREE.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse and litigating.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: £12m remedial programme with c.£7m spent, an unresolved insurance coverage dispute, LD and resident compensation exposure, and insurers holding subrogation rights against the D&B subcontractor Novo.
prospects.routeInNote: Exactly the profile you serve, and directly adverse. Insurance coverage and quantum are the live issues.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Five schemes in dispute with BREE simultaneously (William Gunn House, Block N Vickers, Watermill Lane, Anne Bryan House, Isobel Court), spanning cavity barriers, render non-compliance, HPL and Trespa panels, with a £5.5m portfolio provision under review and a PAS 9980 versus strict Building Regulations battleline.
prospects.routeInNote: On need and capability gap this is the single strongest prospect on the list, and it is the single most conflicted. Reachable only after the BREE portfolio resolves.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Decorum and New Riverside: c.£5m+ cost to complete, a PCSA entered with United Living to design the works, and Tenos design priced at c.£2m to £3m.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse, though the relationship is framed in the tracker as one to preserve.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Revenue £645.6m in the year to 31 March 2026 with a best-ever £18.7m operating profit, net cash £26.4m and an order book above £1bn, 64 per cent of it in orders over £50m. CEO Mark Lawrence left with immediate effect on 14 July 2026 after 40 years. No published disputes, but inherent payment, final account and disruption exposure on fit-out and data centre work is high.
prospects.routeInNote: Would be a first-class client: large, solvent, no in-house forensic function. BREE is currently in adjudication against them on Points Cross.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: c.460 blocks still to assess of almost 1,100; £44m of remediation spend in FY25; no consolidated provision published. Won the Court of Appeal against NHBC on 22 July 2025 over Buildmark Choice indemnity following contractor insolvency. States it will rigorously pursue developers.
prospects.routeInNote: Developer and contractor recovery, and quantification. Created a Director of Asset Investment and Fire Remediation in 2025, so the buyer is identifiable. CHL Developments (legacy Catalyst) sits in this group.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Nine tower blocks placed under 24-hour waking watch in November 2025 after FRAEW found combustible insulation and defective cavity barriers behind glazed curtain walling; £167,000 of waking watch cost to 13 November 2025. £43.255m fire safety within a £0.5bn five-year HRA programme. C3 consumer grade held at 10 June 2026.
prospects.routeInNote: An unbuilt recovery claim against the original contractors and designers of the nine blocks, plus quantification of the remediation. Latent conflict via Adlington Road and Wordsworth Avenue.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Developer remediation contract signatory: 448 buildings in contract, 250 requiring remediation. Added £222m to fire safety provisions on 30 July 2025 (c.£145m for newly found cavity barrier defects behind brickwork and render), taking cladding provision above £434m. Publicly pursuing claims against those responsible for design, workmanship and material failures, with no recoveries assumed in the provision.
prospects.routeInNote: Supply chain recovery programme: causation, forensic quantum of remediation cost, and BSA s.130/s.124 routes. Latent conflict via The Onyx Apartments and Camley Street.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Watling Grange remedials and a spoil and muck-shift dispute subject to a contamination determination, with downstream claims against Howard and JPB. Also a completed non-contentious scheme at Seaview Walk, Murton.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse now, but the tracker's own strategy is a commercial-led solution turning the legals down, so this may clear sooner than most.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Kennaway Estate delay and final account matter, with recovery reduced from c.£5m toward under £1m if delays remain unresolved, plus an emerging works-compliance issue. Optivo is now part of Southern Housing, adding the St Peter's final account dispute.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse on two fronts.

prospects.organisation: Clarion Housing Group (incl. Clarion, Latimer / Dove Lane LLP)
prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: The largest housing association in the country. Adverse through Latimer on Blackfriars Road, but also holds a secured BREE scheme at Gaul Road, a completed regeneration at Ravensbury Estate and a Dove Lane bid.
prospects.routeInNote: The tracker records Clarion four separate ways. High value, but the Blackfriars adjudication makes the whole group conflicted.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: G3 non-compliant governance since 3 January 2024 and still standing at September 2026, with a two-year improvement plan expressly covering commercial processes. £50.3m invested in fire remediation to date. Deficits of £21.0m (FY24) and £12.8m (FY23) before a £116.4m FY25 surplus. Affected by the Ardmore administration.
prospects.routeInNote: Commercial process remediation is named in the regulatory judgement, which is an unusually direct mandate. Latent conflict via Camberwell Road and Wyndham Studios.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: £37m BSA charge in 2025 on top of an £83m provision increase in 2024. Live claims include c.£18m against Unite Students, a £9.6m building liability order claim (25 August 2026), a £34m defects claim on a 2009 job and a £4m developer fire safety claim (6 January 2026).
prospects.routeInNote: Forensic quantum and delay on the BSA and defects portfolio. Note Partner Construction, its Leicester New Build partner, is now owned by Bree Homes Holdings: conflict check required.

prospects.organisation: London Borough of Barnet / Barnet Homes
prospects.organisationType: Local authority and ALMO, c.9,200 homes
prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: 586 homes identified as needing remediation at almost £17m after the Moss Hall Grove fire destroyed four timber-frame homes with 1980s UPVC cladding; £3.6m of council money for 153 council homes. £79.6m of Exceptional Financial Support for 2026-27; budget gap £79.3m rising to £243.5m by 2030/31.
prospects.routeInNote: A defined remediation liability with no identified recovery route, on a council with no money. Latent conflict via Burnt Oak Broadway.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Self-referred to the RSH in April 2025 over fire safety compliance breaches, receiving a C3 on 28 May 2025, described in its own HRA business plan as a significant risk. £2.1m of fire safety works in 2026/27 across 1,208 blocks. £1bn GDV South Kilburn single delivery partner procurement, award estimated 31 May 2026.
prospects.routeInNote: High need, but BREE has a live South Kilburn recovery matter with Network New Build Ltd and Brent is the regeneration authority. Treat as conflicted until scoped.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Section 114 in December 2022 with continuing intervention and £68.91m of Exceptional Financial Support for 2026-27. The £1.4bn Purfleet-on-Thames development agreement with Purfleet Centre Regeneration Ltd was terminated. LGA peer review (December 2025) found an unreliable Decent Homes baseline built on cloned stock data.
prospects.routeInNote: Termination of a £1.4bn development agreement is a live claims and quantum matter in its own right. Latent conflict via Claudian Way.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: FY25 accounts disclose a possible but uncertain obligation to remediate fire safety defects where a PAS 9980 assessment has not been carried out, expressly stated as not reliably estimable. Development target cut c.30 per cent; capital and repairs spend cut from £140.6m to £103.5m in H1 FY26.
prospects.routeInNote: A liability the client says it cannot quantify is the cleanest possible quantum instruction. Latent conflict via Ullesthorpe, Fairway Meadows.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Downgraded G1 to G2 with V2 and a first C2 on 29 October 2025. The RSH found significant overdue fire safety remedial actions, underperformance over a prolonged period resulting in loan write-offs and impairments, and significantly reduced financial flexibility.
prospects.routeInNote: Overdue fire safety remediation plus impairment history points to unrecovered contractor liabilities. Latent conflict via Beaconview Road (Bullock era).

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: G1/V2/C2 at 26 August 2026: repairs service quality and communication weaknesses, difficulty meeting damp and mould demand, and constrained capacity with development part-funded by disposals. Turnover £297m at March 2025.
prospects.routeInNote: Runs a four-year £6.6m Professional Services and Consultancy Framework for the Blue Skies Consortium across 21 lots (awarded 23 April 2024), which is the procurement route. Latent conflict via Tuxford, Ashvale Road.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Two adverse matters: Dumballs Road final account of £1m to £3m with an £800k EWS cladding adjudication, and Outwood Wharf recovery action against Futureserve. Also a secured pipeline scheme at Skinner Street.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse on two fronts. The tracker records Ridgeback separately as a non-contentious counterparty.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Blackfriars Road proceedings of £1m to £3m plus a Latimer and Clarion LD adjudication of c.£1.2m, with settlement expected via mediation.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse. Part of the Clarion group, which also appears twice on the non-contentious side.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Cabinet decision of 3 September 2025 covering 26 higher-risk buildings plus medium-rise blocks, estimated at £15m to £25m over five years against the 2029 deadline, applying to the Cladding Safety Scheme. HRA regeneration programme has stalled after housing association partners withdrew.
prospects.routeInNote: Procures fire remedial works by mini-competition under an existing framework. Latent conflict via Copley Close phases 2 and 4.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Liberty waterproofing dispute with remedial cost of c.£700k to £1.5m, insurers apparently accepting cover subject to a workmanship and design split with a £300k excess.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse, with a without prejudice meeting proposed by end September 2026.

prospects.organisationType: NHS property vehicle and local authority
prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Project Admiral: a five-tower building safety scheme with a £2m residual measured works claim, an accepted £200k LD liability and adjudication planned to start October 2026.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse, with an ancillary dispute with RKC on Project Admiral and Sterte Court.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Kingston Heights Hotel: combustible insulation, cavity barriers, spandrels and defective STO render, with Court proceedings underway, no solvent downstream and a Part 36 settlement of £1m to £1.5m targeted.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse and litigating.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Wisbech Road boilers and insurance claim heading to adjudication or Court against Top Rank, with claim preparation targeted for end August 2026.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse. One of the largest affordable housing investors in the country, so high future value once clear.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: £931.1m HRA capital over five years; £6.7m a year for structural inspection requirements under the Building Safety Act plus £4.2m for building safety works. Re-tendering c.£596m of housing repairs and maintenance as a Strategic Alliance, including compliance and professional services frameworks, with tenders expected from early 2026.
prospects.routeInNote: The professional services framework is a live, dated route in. Latent conflict via Daventry House.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: G1/V1 with a C2 consumer grade from the September 2025 inspection (judgement 24 September 2025). Completions fell short of target as repairs demand was prioritised. Turnover £233.7m FY26.
prospects.routeInNote: Two secured BREE schemes (Esh Winning, Pelton Fell) give a current live relationship, which is both the warmest access route here and the sharpest latent conflict.

prospects.organisation: Midland Heart (incl. Midland Heart Developments Limited)
prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: G1/V1/C1, the highest available, Moody's A1. Completions down 56 per cent to 356 in FY26 while investment in existing homes rose to a record £55m. Target raised to 2,750 homes by 2030 on c.£300m of investment.
prospects.routeInNote: Seven tracker schemes across Midland Heart and Midland Heart Developments, including two secured. Financially the strongest mid-tier buyer with the warmest existing relationship.

prospects.organisation: Platform Housing Group (incl. Platform New Homes, formerly ESHA (Developments))
prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Three high-rise buildings in Worcester found not fully to meet building safety standards, with mitigations and independent expert and fire authority confirmation that they remain safe to occupy. 1,380 completions FY26, up 34 per cent, with c.1,600 starts planned for 2026/27.
prospects.routeInNote: Note: the tracker's 'ESHA (Developments) Limited' is now Platform New Homes, and 'Platform Housing' and 'Platform Housing Group' are the same group. Five tracker schemes in total, so a strong but conflicted relationship.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: The LLP's accounts to 31 March 2025 indicate it is dormant and not trading, with trading apparently in CZWG Limited. Southwark is reported to have issued a c.£5m High Court claim in June 2025 over defects at Canada Water Library.
prospects.routeInNote: A multi-million claim against a practice filing dormant LLP accounts raises acute PI cover, run-off and entity questions. BREE is adjudicating against them for c.£2m on Welbourne.

prospects.organisation: Livv Housing Group (formerly Knowsley Housing Trust / First Ark)
prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Five high-rise buildings in BSA scope. Four blocks at Gaywood Green, Kirkby (256 flats) were demolished after health and safety issues and Merseyside Fire and Rescue concerns. Restructured and rebranded in 2020 following a 2018 RSH non-compliance finding on fire safety.
prospects.routeInNote: Demolition of 256 flats implies an unpursued recovery. Fusion21's £175m Construction Consultancy Services Framework is the local procurement vehicle. Latent conflict via Bluebell Park.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: C3 at 30 October 2024: c.2 per cent of required asbestos management surveys completed at March 2024, no asbestos re-inspection register despite a September 2023 contractor recommendation, over 14,000 overdue repairs with 90 per cent unassigned. 55 high-rise blocks containing c.3,040 flats, with nine still to be prioritised.
prospects.routeInNote: Nine unaddressed high-rise blocks and a £45m five-year package. Latent conflict via West Road and Ladbury Road (Bullock era).

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: The largest developing association in the UK: 2,871 completions FY26, turnover £945.6m, surplus £185.7m, liquidity £1.23bn, Moody's A2 and S&P A+. Only 10 higher-risk buildings in BSA scope across the combined group.
prospects.routeInNote: Low building safety exposure but very high development volume, so the value is in NEC and JCT final accounts, delay and contractor insolvency on a £18bn to 2040 programme. Latent conflict via Weavers Close, Peterlee, North Pickenham Road, Walton on the Naze, Wheaters Meadow, Tower Mill and The Moorings.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Centrica Business Solutions adjusted operating profit £47m in FY25, down from £73m. Real exposure sits in heat network and energy centre EPC delivery and in social housing heating workmanship. Large in-house legal team but limited construction forensic capability.
prospects.routeInNote: BREE has issued an initial notice and is preparing a PAP or Court claim against Centrica on Decorum.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Turnover down 16 per cent to £29.5m in the year to 31 March 2025 with pre-tax profit down about 80 per cent to £267,000, average employee numbers cut by 49, and LLP cash down to £193,668 from £1,063,043. Real 30-year retrospective DPA exposure through high-rise residential and student work.
prospects.routeInNote: Acute need and no in-house forensic capability, but BREE is suing them as a defendant on Wenlock, with the strike-out heard on 21 and 22 July 2026.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: LGAH turnover £204m FY25, up 33.8 per cent, 6,700 homes rising to c.7,700 by end 2026, but swung to a £24.2m pre-tax loss on a £50m portfolio revaluation loss. The affordable housing fund has raised over £750m since July 2024. L&G Modular Homes was wound down with cumulative losses of £174m.
prospects.routeInNote: Institutional capacity to pay and a build partner model that generates final account and defect risk. Latent conflict via Sampson Green.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Planned turnover around £70m with 99 employees, shareholders' funds £10.49m and cash £5.37m. Communal housing is its largest project sector at 40 projects, carrying fire-stopping and BSA exposure. No in-house forensic capability at this scale.
prospects.routeInNote: BREE has two live adjudications against LJJ on Welbourne (c.£300k and c.£2m). Note also a separate LJJ Contractors Ltd incorporated in 2024.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: 146 employees and shareholders' funds of £7.24m at 31 October 2025. Twelve public contracts of c.£973.6m awarded value including Fusion21 and local authority frameworks. Building surveying, QS, employer's agent, project management and fire engineering, but no evident forensic quantum, delay or expert witness team.
prospects.routeInNote: BREE is pursuing recovery against them on Liberty, with a without prejudice meeting proposed by end September 2026.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: G1/V1/C1. Owns and manages homes in a range of tall buildings with an FRA programme including planned works and mitigating actions, but publishes no provision or buildings-in-scope count. Turnover £230.4m FY25, 650 completions.
prospects.routeInNote: Unquantified tall building exposure on a financially strong balance sheet. Latent conflict via Darlington, Alexander Street.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: C2 at 25 March 2026: fire safety management assessed as effective, but 9 per cent of homes have overdue electrical safety tests and 9 per cent fail Decent Homes, with stock condition surveys due to complete by August 2027. Affordable Housing Strategy 2026 to 2036 targets 1,500 homes a year by 2036.
prospects.routeInNote: Launched a c.£1.5bn framework tender on 30 October 2025 and a c.£5m cost consultancy framework. Latent conflict via Holbeck Living and Meynell Approach; note the tracker also misspells this as 'Leed City Council'.

prospects.organisation: Network Homes / Network New Build Ltd
prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: South Kilburn brickwork, waterproofing and window defects with a United Living scope of c.£300k within the insurance excess. Also two completed schemes (Kilburn Quarters, Evergreen Gardens) and Ridgeway Sele Farm.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse. The tracker records Network Homes and Network New Build Ltd separately: confirm whether they are the same group.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Settlement of c.£400k plus a prior offer, with the status of a previous payment to be confirmed and the future NHBC relationship being weighed.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse. Note Peabody's Court of Appeal win against NHBC on 22 July 2025 on Buildmark Choice indemnity, which reshapes this area.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: St Peter's (Greenlands and Silverlands) final account and EOT dispute with practical completion not yet granted, with adjudication preparation to be finalised by around September 2026. Status queried in the Spotlight review of 26 July 2026.
prospects.routeInNote: Now part of Southern Housing, so treat the conflict at group level.

prospects.organisation: Orbit Group / Orbit Homes (incl. Orbit Homes (2020))
prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: G1/V2 at the December 2025 stability check, V2 because cost pressures alongside the development and sales programme reduce financial capacity. Target raised to 7,000 homes by 2030 with 60 per cent direct build.
prospects.routeInNote: Moving to 60 per cent direct build sharply increases its exposure to final accounts, delay and subcontractor insolvency. Five tracker schemes, four of them Bullock era.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: L&Q's in-house contracting and development delivery company, registered at L&Q's office. Full accounts to 31 March 2025 filed, no charges and no insolvency filings. L&Q funds in full the remediation of the 1,100 homes built by Quadrant.
prospects.routeInNote: Approach as part of the L&Q group rather than separately. Latent conflict via South Thames College.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Ardmore Construction Ltd entered administration on 28 August 2025, blaming the BSA's retrospective extension of Defective Premises Act limitation from 12 to 30 years. Six cladding claims of over £150m in its final year, £85m already spent on remediation. Administrators record £91.4m of cladding claims from 16 creditors and £204.4m of potential claims against subcontractors, against total estimated debts above £500m and an expected 7.68 per cent dividend.
prospects.routeInNote: The largest forensic recovery exercise on this list, but BREE has a live D&B claim against Ardmore on Paynes and Borthwick and ACL cannot pay. Group survives and forecasts over £400m revenue in 2026.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: G1/V2/C2 (25 September 2024). Record 1,280 completions and 1,647 starts in FY26 with capital commitments of £526.3m. £5.5m of safety investment FY25, mainly detection. No cladding provision published.
prospects.routeInNote: Volume development risk rather than legacy building safety. No BREE project in the tracker, so among the cleanest routes.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: G2/V2 at January 2026 and C2 from 18 December 2024. The RSH cites internal control weaknesses identified in 2023, insufficient board assurance, weak business planning and stress testing, and cost pressures where planned savings are not evidenced. Post-tax surplus £2.9m FY24 after a £4.4m FY23 deficit.
prospects.routeInNote: Three completed BREE schemes (Johnson House Bootle, Johnsons Cleaners HQ, Carr Lane Prescot) give a warm route but also the latent conflict.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Residential-led practice whose portfolio (affordable housing, estate regeneration, later living) is precisely the stock now subject to remediation and building liability orders, giving it among the highest ratios of retrospective liability to balance sheet on this list. No adjudications or PI claims reported.
prospects.routeInNote: BREE holds a downstream claim against PTE on Arundel Square, with a limited covenant and a standstill recorded to 30 September 2025.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Control passed from Partner Group U.K. Limited to Bree Homes Holdings Limited in August 2025. Residential SIC code means real BSA exposure if it has built above 11 metres. Accounts to 31 March 2025 filed; no identifiable in-house claims capability.
prospects.routeInNote: Now a BREE group company, so this is internal work rather than a prospect. The tracker records it three ways: Partner Construction, Partner Construction Ltd, and Partner Construction / Balfour Beatty.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Garden Walk notification, with Mostyn Bullock rating copper cladding with PIR core and rendered masonry low risk and curtain walling medium.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse but at risk-evaluation stage only, and the exposure may narrow to nothing. Strong covenant, so high value once clear.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Arundel Square RPML cavity barrier defect claim under the Building Safety Act with a Remediation Contribution Order in play, dating from November 2009 works, with H+H close to persuading ASDL's expert to a sprinkler solution.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse. An RCO claim is precisely the Building Safety Act pillar work.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Alsecco EWI system claim from 2012 works, with counsel advising defences are available but settlement recommended, a BS8414 test planned and the claimant accessing the Building Safety Fund.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Target of BREE's recovery action on Outwood Wharf, with litigation or adjudication estimated at 3 to 6 months from PROMEP access.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Downstream claim on Kennaway Estate of £400k to £800k, to be valued by end September 2026.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Parkview: works suspended on health and safety grounds, default notice and termination strategy prepared, completion offer underwritten by the GLA.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse, with termination live.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Beaufort Park balcony design solution with sprinkler discussions, at design, delivery and cost risk evaluation stage.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse but early stage.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Downgraded to G1/V2/C2 on 27 August 2025. Predominantly low-rise stock, so building safety exposure appears modest. Turnover £306.1m FY25; £100m funding package secured in H1 FY26. Procures an external legal services framework.
prospects.routeInNote: Development and final account work rather than building safety. Latent conflict via Wellingborough.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Target of adjudication or Court proceedings on the Wisbech Road boilers and insurance claim.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Ipswich (Sandyhills) adjudication, with Sean Ellison valuing by end August 2026 and settlement then adjudication from July 2026.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Fire strategies authored on pre-2017 high-rise schemes now sit within the 30-year retrospective limitation period, and fire engineers are routinely drawn into cladding litigation (see Greater Glasgow Health Board v Multiplex [2025] CSOH 56). Small specialist practice, no in-house forensic quantum or delay.
prospects.routeInNote: Currently instructed on the other side of BREE matters (REQ on Kingston Heights, design on Decorum). Adviser and adjacent competitor, not a prospect.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: G1/V2 at 17 December 2025, the V2 because investment in quality and safety alongside new development reduces capacity for adverse events. Minimal building safety exposure on low-rise County Durham stock. 208 completions FY25 across 13 sites.
prospects.routeInNote: Two tracker schemes (Weavers Close, Peterlee). Note the tracker records this entity twice, as 'believe housing' and 'Believe Housing'.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Launched Building Safety Act Services and Fire Safety Services in 2023, and names expert witness and due diligence among its service lines. Heavy affordable housing and employer's agent workload creates genuine PI and BSA exposure as a consultant defendant.
prospects.routeInNote: BREE is adjudicating against them on three Newlon schemes and has issued protective proceedings on a fourth. Also part-competitor: it has BSA and expert witness capability in house.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Part of CK Asset Holdings. Chelsea Waterfront (Lots Road) East Tower completing 2025 and Convoys Wharf Deptford consented. Development risk sits in project SPVs; accounts to 31 December 2024 filed with no insolvency notices.
prospects.routeInNote: Very strong covenant but no evidenced dispute need. Latent conflict via Lots Road.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Architect claim or adjudication on Watling Grange, awaiting David Halford's liability advice.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Small practice filing under the small companies regime with £20,000 share capital and ten directors. Architect cover on Newlon Block N is limited to £130k. Sports, stadia and leisure focus means lower residential BSA exposure than the housing practices.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse on Newlon Block N. Note this is unrelated to the US firm KSS Architects.

prospects.organisation: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham / Be First
prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Be First is developing c.3,000 units across c.60 schemes on c.£2bn of capital investment. MTFS 2026-27 shows a £12.6m gap rising to £16.8m by 2028/29, and warns Be First schemes transferred to Reside over 50-year financing may no longer generate sufficient returns to offset financing costs.
prospects.routeInNote: A £2bn programme whose financing model the council itself now questions. Latent conflict via Grays Court and Becontree Avenue.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: HRA General Reserve of £4.9m at 31 March 2025 against a recommended minimum of £16.7m. New build programme re-phased with a £14.1m reduction to the 2025/26 budget. £40m of borrowing headroom earmarked for building safety and Decent Homes 2, with emerging building safety requirements flagged as a live risk.
prospects.routeInNote: Under-reserved HRA with unquantified emerging building safety cost. Latent conflict via Sparrow Farm.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Protective proceedings issued against SERS on Newlon Anne Bryan House on 15 November 2024.
prospects.routeInNote: Adverse and in proceedings.

prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Underwriting the completion offer on Parkview, with a commercial meeting planned for September 2026.
prospects.routeInNote: A funder rather than a disputing party, but a significant future client for programme assurance and claims scrutiny.

prospects.organisation: Hedyn (formerly Newport City Homes, merged with Melin)
prospects.whyTheyNeedYou: Merged with Melin Homes to form Hedyn from 1 April 2025. £37m five-year Newport city centre regeneration programme creating c.160 homes across seven sites, announced 21 July 2026. Welsh Government assessment of September 2026 gave green ratings across the board.
prospects.routeInNote: Wales sits under the Building Safety (Wales) Act 2026, not the BSA 2022, so the building safety pillar does not transfer. Latent conflict via Pillgwenlly Regeneration.
